findings.title: Video references lose the credential needed for cancellation
findings.body: The non-calendar branch now stores an undefined credentialId instead of result.credentialId. Newly created bookings using connected video apps therefore lose the credential associated with their meeting. handleCancelBooking only deletes a video meeting when its reference contains a credentialId, so cancelling these bookings leaves the external meeting alive. Seat cancellation also skips updating these references. Preserve result.credentialId for video results.

findings.title: Non-Google co-host events target the organizer's calendar
findings.body: Each destination's credential receives the complete, unchanged destinationCalendar array. Office365CalendarService, LarkCalendarService, and BaseCalendarService still select the first array item rather than the destination associated with that credential. For example, an Office365 co-host following a Google organizer sends the organizer's Google address as a Microsoft calendar ID, causing creation to fail. CalDAV can instead filter out every calendar and report success without creating anything. Route each creation to the current credential's destination.

findings.title: Non-Google calendar IDs are sent as Google attendee emails
findings.body: The organizer attendee's email is taken from the first destination's externalId regardless of its integration. In a collective event with an Office365 organizer and a Google co-host, that value is a Microsoft calendar ID, not an email address. Google rejects the co-host's event with an invalid attendee email even though the target calendar is correctly selected by credentialId later. The same problem exists in updateEvent. Only substitute an appropriate Google calendar email; otherwise retain the organizer's email.

findings.title: An empty destination list crashes the Google Meet fallback
findings.body: destinationCalendar is optional, nullable, and can be empty, so destructuring it can leave mainHostDestinationCalendar undefined. Accessing its integration without optional chaining throws when a Google Meet event has no destination calendar—the exact case this fallback is intended to handle. Booking creation or confirmation now fails instead of switching to Cal Video. Preserve the previous null-safe check.

findings.title: Co-host calendars are discarded when the organizer has none
findings.body: When neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, evt.destinationCalendar is initialized to null. The optional push then silently discards all calendars collected from the other collective hosts. A collective booking with an unconnected organizer and a connected co-host consequently never passes the co-host's calendar or credential to EventManager, so nothing is created in that host's destination calendar. Initialize an array before adding the co-host destinations.

findings.title: Legacy Google destinations are silently redirected to primary
findings.body: EventManager explicitly supports destinations without a credentialId by selecting credentials using the integration name. In that path, this lookup cannot match a destination's null credentialId to the numeric credentialId argument. Google therefore inserts into primary instead of the configured externalId. Existing configurations targeting a secondary or shared calendar silently start writing bookings to the wrong calendar. Retain destination-based routing for the legacy integration-selection path.

findings.title: Missing reference calendar IDs no longer use the destination fallback
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is null or undefined, the fallback searches for a destination whose string externalId equals that missing value, so it cannot find one. This replaces the previous fallback to the configured destination and calls Google update without its required calendarId. The equivalent lookup in deleteEvent instead falls back to primary, where a secondary-calendar event returns a 404 that is treated as successful deletion. Bookings with missing reference calendar IDs can no longer reschedule correctly and can leave calendar events behind after cancellation.

findings.title: Deferred confirmation loses collective co-host destinations
findings.body: handleNewBooking persists only the first destination calendar on Booking. When a collective booking requires confirmation, this handler reconstructs the event using only that stored destination or the confirming user's destination; it never restores the other hosts' calendars. EventManager's new creation loop therefore receives only one destination and writes only that host's calendar event. Rebuild the participating hosts' destinations before deferred calendar creation. The payment webhook event builders have the same single-destination limitation.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation ignores the resolved co-host credential
findings.body: For cancellation of all remaining recurrences, this branch ignores the calendar credential just resolved for the current reference and iterates only the organizer's credentials. It also selects only the first calendar reference from each recurrence. With multiple host references, the outer loop consequently repeats deletion of the organizer's events but never deletes the co-host's events using their own credentials. All bookings are marked cancelled while the co-host's calendar remains occupied. Process each recurrence's references with their associated credentials.

findings.title: Reschedule requests use one user's credential for every host
findings.body: Collective bookings now contain calendar references for multiple hosts, but requestReschedule still resolves references through a map keyed only by integration type and populated from the requesting user's credentials. Two Google hosts' references are therefore both deleted using one host's Google token; references for co-host integrations absent from the map are skipped entirely. The booking is already marked cancelled, and deletion failures are swallowed, so requesting a reschedule leaves co-host events blocking their calendars. Resolve each reference using its credentialId.

findings.title: Organization creation drops the slug when billing is disabled
findings.body: This reverses the original condition for saving the organization slug. When IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is false, creation now saves neither slug nor metadata.requestedSlug, despite provisioning or announcing the domain using the requested slug earlier in the handler. Newly created organizations on billing-disabled installations therefore cannot resolve at their requested organization address. Preserve the original negated condition for slug.
